summary: The claim follows from the accepted decreasing-score theorem by an exact affine unimodular transformation. The integer anchor ratios and integer capacity give a bijection of the complete supports, including all boundary atoms. The inverse formulas, score identity, and normalizer identity are correct. Every transformed score is nonpositive, and the dimension, capacity, positive resource coefficients, support, probabilities, depth convention, and constants meet the accepted theorem's hypotheses. The invertible affine map bijects containing closed halfspaces and preserves their masses, so the depth and third moment are exactly invariant. The cases n=1, Q=0, tied score-per-cost ratios, and lattice coordinates forced to zero are covered. The unit-cost corollary follows for every stated finite real score vector.
